xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5621: Gate admission queue starves indefinitely when MemAvailable stays below hard reserve + footprint; idle parked workspace stacks are never reclaimed

plan.title: Gate admission queue starves indefinitely when MemAvailable stays below hard reserve + footprint; idle parked workspace stacks are never reclaimed
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The plan touches 20 files. The lint counts 8 subsystems only because each top-level doc file (docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md, configuration/memory-governor.mdx, changelog.d/pan-5621.md) and each test root (tests/lib, tests/unit) is its own subsystem. The code surface is src/lib (cloister and config-yaml), one primary-dashboard service and one pan status line. The separable half of the issue (FR-2, reclaiming parked stacks) is already split to PAN-5623.

narratives.Problem: The quality-gate admission queue can stall indefinitely and silently. When no gate holds a slot and MemAvailable stays below the governor's hard reserve plus the head gate's footprint, the PAN-5285 alone-admission can never fire, so no gate ever starts. On 2026-11-23 the PAN-5489 typecheck head waited 52 minutes with 7 waiters behind it (MemAvailable 8.5-10.4 GB, hard reserve 8 GiB, footprint 2,864,852,992 bytes). Nothing reported it until the Flywheel read the waiter files and stopped containers by hand.
narratives.Proposal: A primary-dashboard service, src/dashboard/server/services/gate-starvation-service.ts, polls every 30 s. It reads the read-only queue snapshot, which gains three things: ticketId, footprintKey and memoryBlockedSince on entries; readError (an unreadable queue is unknown, never empty); and lastAdmittedAt, from a best-effort last-admitted.json marker that every admission writes. It evaluates a pure predicate in src/lib/cloister/gate-starvation.ts: starved iff there is no owner, the head has been memory-blocked for at least resources.quality_gate_starvation_minutes (default 15), and the head does not fit alone above the hard reserve, using the same helper admission now uses. The first starved poll opens an episode in ~/.overdeck/verification-workers/admission/starvation.json with announced:false, sends one phone push (best-effort, stable tag) and one settled emitActivityEntryOnce warning (stable id). The warning is retried until it settles, even across restarts. A new head hands the episode over with refreshed figures. The episode closes on progress (an owner, or a marker at or after opening) or on a confirmed empty queue: the record is marked closing, a settled recovery entry is sent, and only then is the record deleted. pan status prints one line while the episode is open. Docs: docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md, configuration/memory-governor.mdx, changelog.d/pan-5621.md. FR-2 (reclaiming parked workspace stacks) moved to PAN-5623.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No automatic stopping, restarting or reclaiming of any container or process; that is PAN-5623
- No dashboard Needs-you card, new HTTP route, contracts type or frontend change
- No change to any admission decision (FIFO, passing, alone-admission, CPU bypass, reserve arithmetic)
- No starvation detection while any gate holds a slot; a stuck or long-running owner is not starvation
- No starvation for tickets older than PAN-5285 (no memoryBlockedSince) or heads without a footprintKey
- No change to the pan status --json output shape
- No change to src/lib/cloister/idle-stack-reaper.ts (its full-stack label bug is reported on #3050)
- No detection on remote (Fly) machines
- No allowlist cap raise in scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt
- No guaranteed phone delivery and no new push outcome API (the push is best-effort; the settled activity entry, the record and pan status are the guaranteed surfaces)
- No close on a short admission by a pre-PAN-5621 checkout that writes no admission marker

autoDecisions.summary: Split FR-2 (reclaim parked workspace stacks) into sibling issue PAN-5623
autoDecisions.rationale: No path restarts a stack for a live parked pane: rebuildWorkspaceStack runs only at spawn, on infraUnavailable gates and from the CLI. Stopped containers read as STACK BROKEN. The work overlaps PAN-5250's restart-on-demand. Combined with FR-1 it exceeds the 25-file plan limit.

autoDecisions.summary: Surface the episode through pan status, one activity entry and one phone push (pushNeedsYouEdge), not a new dashboard Needs-you card
autoDecisions.rationale: A card needs a route, a contracts type and frontend components (about 12 files) for a rare event that the existing Needs-you push channel already delivers.

autoDecisions.summary: Run detection in a primary-dashboard service, not in waiters or the deacon child
autoDecisions.rationale: It gives a single writer for the announcement. pushNeedsYouEdge works only in the primary. PAN-5623's reclaim needs the runtime mirror that only the main process holds.

autoDecisions.summary: A live slot owner suppresses detection, and an episode ends only when an owner appears or the queue empties
autoDecisions.rationale: A running gate means the queue moves, and alone-admission needs empty slots anyway. Tying the end to progress stops head rotation (30-minute wrapper timeouts) and flapping MemAvailable from re-announcing.

autoDecisions.summary: resources.quality_gate_starvation_minutes is valid above 0 and under 30, default 15, global config only
autoDecisions.rationale: It mirrors quality_gate_cpu_bypass_minutes and stays under the 30-minute wrapper admission wait, so a wrapper-run head is reported before it times out.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4 with D1, D2, D4, D5, D7 and D8. Create gate-starvation-service.ts, mirroring disk-alert-service.ts: injectable deps (emitOnce = emitActivityEntryOnce, push = pushNeedsYouEdge), a 30 s interval, an in-flight guard and timer.unref(). Poll: (1) a snapshot with readError returns, leaving the record untouched. (2) A closing record: if never announced, clear; else emitOnce the recovery (id gate-starvation:<since>:recovered) and clear only when the outcome is not 'failed'. (3) An open record: on a close reason, write closing and settle as in (2). Else, if not announced, push (tag gate-starvation:<since>) and emitOnce the warning (id gate-starvation:<since>:opened), and set announced:true when settled. On a changed head ticket, refresh that head's estimate, MemAvailable and hard reserve and rewrite the record without emitting. (4) No record: evaluate; when starved, collect holders (failure gives []), write the record with announced:false, then announce. Wire start and stop next to the disk-alert service in main.ts (primary only). Tests use fake timers only.

items.title: Under fake timers, a head memory-blocked for 14 min produces no emit; past 15 min, exactly one emitOnce with id gate-starvation:<since>:opened and one push with tag gate-starvation:<since> occur, the record ends announced:true, and five further polls add none

When emitOnce returns 'failed' then 'appended', the record stays announced:false after poll 1 and becomes announced:true after poll 2 with the same id; a restarted service finding an announced:false record emits the opening id once and marks it announced

A snapshot with no owner, a new head and lastAdmittedAt after openedAtMs writes closing.reason 'admitted', emits the recovery id saying 'a gate was admitted', and clears the record; a failed recovery emit keeps the closing record until a later poll settles it
